subject: C30
required_fixes: R1 — High: crates/desktop-core/src/authority/observation_domain.rs:216, :232, :246 and :499 conflate a tenant's cached record with its current in-flight context. record_for overwrites context without separating or clearing the old in_flight count. If A has an outstanding read, switches A→B→A before that work settles, and snoozes a cached item or starts another read, record_for assigns A's new context. The old completion then cannot find its record in retired_part_done; the leaked count can leave ReadStatus permanently reading and disable Read now. Keep cached tenant data independent of per-operation/context bookkeeping. Acceptance: deterministically delay an old read's cancellation/settlement, round-trip tenants and snooze/start a new read before releasing it; all parts settle once, refreshing clears, generations count only valid completions, and the retired reply never replaces cached data.

R2 — High: crates/desktop-core/src/authority/observation_domain.rs:350–367 counts Red Team scans, model scans and skill scans as complete merely because their Option is Some. Their production types in crates/desktop-core/src/red_team.rs carry complete/capped flags, and the finite reads return only their first page. A capped or truncated inventory therefore becomes ProductReadState::Ok with no missing coverage and can produce an ok 'all sources complete' toast, contrary to I4/T13. Preserve these completeness flags in read outcomes and truthful partial-source counts; bounded reads need not fetch the entire inventory. Acceptance: production-interface fixtures with total greater than returned rows, capped counts and incomplete model/skill pages yield incomplete coverage and a warn completion; complete pages remain ok. Count missing sources rather than aggregated product-label strings.

R3 — High: crates/desktop-core/src/authority/inbox_domain.rs:385 checks absence of successful data before overview.failure, and apps/desktop/src/v2/home.tsx:20 checks lastReadAt before failure. An admitted first read that fails during binding/token acquisition records a failure and completion generation but remains 'First read pending', with pending product entries. apps/desktop/src/v2/inbox/inbox.tsx:86 also maps a failed empty read to 'Nothing needs action'. Independently exercising the production presentation reproduced both misleading messages. Distinguish never attempted, in progress, failed, partial and healthy empty reads throughout core/Home/Inbox. Acceptance: an admitted first-read authentication/transport failure yields an explicit failed status and meaningful warn toast, never pending or an unqualified all-clear; retry can recover, and failed refreshes label retained successful data as older.

R4 — High: apps/desktop/src/v2/store.ts:7–20, :72–78 and apps/desktop/src/v2/v2-shell.tsx:236–282 keep contextual arrivals and unconfirmed item actions globally, without tenant ownership or current-context filtering. After following A's API-key item, switching to B and opening Administration, B receives A's persisted arrival.item as its initial filter. An unknown snooze/acknowledgment from A likewise remains displayed with its item title and Retry in B. Rust's stale-context check prevents that retry from borrowing B's authority, but the presentation still leaks/misattributes A's item state, violating I2. Scope/consume these surfaces by their originating tenant and retire obsolete action authority. Acceptance: exercise A→B→A with a contextual target and unknown item delivery; B never inherits A's filter or item action surface, while any restored A presentation cannot revive or silently rebind its retired intent.

R5 — Medium: crates/desktop-core/src/authority/harness_history.rs:751–757 discards history::delete's result and reports Discarded even when removal returns HistoryFailure::Unavailable. The switch has already been admitted, so 'Discard and switch' can silently leave a previously saved transcript readable after returning or relaunching. Treat an absent record as already removed, but retain and surface real deletion failures with a recoverable cleanup outcome. Acceptance: inject a deletion I/O/access failure for an existing saved conversation; the UI never implies successful discard, the failure remains observable after switching, and an explicit successful recovery removes the record. Keep the existing Archive-versus-Discard happy-path test.
